subject.title: feat(agents): configured agent env reaches spawned subprocesses

question: Should OpenClaw accept broad literal `agents.list[].env` propagation to CLI, gateway exec, ACP/ACPX, and stdio MCP child processes, or should the canonical solution be the narrower exec-only SecretRef model from #96309?
rationale: Both branches can address real operator needs, but they define different public config, credential, and subprocess-boundary contracts that automation should not choose without maintainer intent.

options.title: Choose one env contract first
options.body: Use maintainer review to pick the canonical broad-env or exec-only SecretRef direction, then merge only the branch that matches that decision.

options.title: Accept broad agent env
options.body: Merge this PR after current checks refresh if maintainers are comfortable making `agents.list[].env` a literal child-process config contract across all wired subprocess families.

options.title: Prefer exec-only SecretRefs
options.body: Pause or close this PR and route the remaining work through #96309 if maintainers want credentials limited to gateway exec with SecretRef handling.

recommendation.title: Choose one env contract first
recommendation.body: Use maintainer review to pick the canonical broad-env or exec-only SecretRef direction, then merge only the branch that matches that decision.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available routing signal for the changed agent config, exec, and ACPX surfaces plus prior review context.
